evals.prompt: Build a pricing card and a primary button in the Neo-Brutalism style using Tailwind v4. The project has no existing design system.
evals.expected_output: A pricing card and button that use the neo-brutalism token block through the --ui-* roles and the @theme inline mapping, with a visible focus ring and no hard-coded colours.
expectations: Uses the neo-brutalism token block via the .theme-neo-brutalism class and --ui-* roles instead of hard-coded hex values
Uses `@theme inline` (not a plain `@theme` and not a JS theme.extend) for the Tailwind v4 mapping
Includes a visible :focus-visible style and does not clip the focusable element
Handles prefers-reduced-motion for the press-offset hover effect
Does not claim a contrast ratio it did not take from the ledger or recompute

evals.prompt: Our app already has a design system with CSS variables --brand-bg, --brand-card and --brand-ink. Add a glassmorphism control bar to the dashboard header.
evals.expected_output: A glass control bar mapped onto the existing variables, without replacing the existing design system, with the glass backdrop requirements and fallbacks.
expectations: Maps the --ui-* roles onto the existing --brand-* variables (or uses them directly) and does not replace the existing design system
States or ensures the glass surface sits over a dark or saturated backdrop, and keeps the tint so white text stays legible over a light backdrop
Provides an @supports fallback for missing backdrop-filter and handles prefers-reduced-transparency
Uses a focus ring that is visible on both light and dark backdrops (two-tone or equivalent)
Does not add global .ui-card / .ui-button rules that would affect existing components

evals.prompt: I'm launching an online pharmacy. Pick a visual style for the site and explain why.
evals.expected_output: A reasoned proposal of a primary and secondary style for a healthcare-adjacent product, avoiding styles the product-fit table lists as wrong for it.
expectations: Proposes a primary and a secondary style with one reason each, using Best for and Avoid when guidance
Does not propose maximalism, cyberpunk or another style the table lists under Avoid for healthcare

Says the table has no exact online-pharmacy row and that it is working from the nearest analogue (the Healthcare or clinic row, or general e-commerce), instead of presenting its answer as an exact catalog match
Mentions at least one relevant risk or requirement from the style index (for example inputs needing the --ui-border)
Gives a recommendation with reasons and risk only, and does not write CSS or token files because the user didn't ask for them

evals.prompt: Make my site look like a Memphis-design 1980s postmodern poster with confetti shapes and zigzags.
evals.expected_output: An honest statement that no indexed style matches Memphis design, with the two closest styles clearly labelled as unverified, not presented as catalog guidance.
expectations: States that there is no verified match in the catalog for this style
Labels the two closest styles (for example maximalism and y2k or scrapbook) as unverified suggestions
If it creates a Memphis token block anyway, it labels it unverified, keeps it out of the catalog, and does not claim contrast was verified for it
If it proceeds to build anything, it takes colours from an indexed style's tokens or recomputes contrast and says so

evals.prompt: Add a Minimalism-style invoice summary card with a Pay button and a Download link to our existing dashboard page. The app already styles its own body, headings and buttons, so don't touch those. You can't open a browser here.
evals.expected_output: A scoped card (no page-level rules), controls with explicit types, contrast pairs taken from the ledger or recomputed for the surface actually used, and an honest statement that nothing was rendered.
expectations: Writes no rule whose selector is a bare html, body, * or element name, including inside media queries
Gives every button an explicit type, and uses a real link for Download
Quotes a contrast ratio only for a pair that is in the ledger on that surface, or one it recomputed, and does not reuse a ledger ratio for the same colour on a different surface
Says it did not render the result and leaves the render-only checklist items open, instead of writing rendered or checked in a browser
Shows both relative luminances beside any ratio it computes, and lists the result of searching its own files for http(s):// before it states its dependencies or fonts
Applies the same scoping rule to any demo page it builds, including the inline style block

evals.prompt: Our product page for a pair of headphones feels flat and people don't know what to tap. Rebuild the hero in the Swiss style: product name, photo, price, colour swatches and an Add to bag button. No browser is available.
evals.expected_output: A Swiss-themed hero that applies the composition moves: a decorative oversized back word behind the product photo with controls on top, the accent reserved for interactive elements, and one huge element with small supporting text, all within the contrast, focus and scoping contracts.
expectations: Reads references/composition.md and names which moves it applied and why
The oversized back word is aria-hidden and the product name also exists as real text, or its contrast is recomputed at every backdrop it crosses
The product image cannot intercept clicks (pointer-events: none or equivalent) and no control or body text is overlapped
--ui-accent appears only on interactive elements and their states, not on the price, headings, swatches' decoration or the back word
Uses one huge element with body text at least 16px and labels at least 12px, and keeps a logical heading order
Says it did not render the result and leaves the overlap, reflow and 200% zoom checks open

evals.prompt: Build me a SaaS landing page for Ledgerline, an invoicing tool for freelance illustrators. Sections: hero, how it works, pricing (Free and Studio at 12 euro a month), and a footer with Contact and Privacy. No customer names, quotes or usage numbers exist yet. No browser is available.
evals.expected_output: A landing page in an indexed style that carries none of the anti-slop tells, with the delivery note reporting the rubric run (version, counts by id and severity), the five Could-this-be-any-site answers with evidence, and tells kept out of any ux-laws finding.
expectations: Reads references/anti-slop.md and names the rubric version (v1) in the delivery note
The hero is not a centred H1, one line and two buttons: one huge element, one accent-filled action, and the second action as an outline or a text link
No three-column icon-card grid, no purple-to-blue gradient, no gradient text, no hero badge, no blurred colour blobs and no section that fades in on scroll
No trusted-by logo row, testimonial cards or stat tiles, because the brief supplied no customers, quotes or figures; the pricing tiers are the only parallel grid, and the brief asked for them
The footer holds only Contact and Privacy, with no placeholder link columns
Headline and calls to action name the product and the audience (invoicing, illustrators) and use verb plus object, not Get started or Learn more alone
Answers the five Could-this-be-any-site questions, one sentence of evidence each, under their own heading in the delivery note
Reports tell counts per page by id and severity with zero high and at most two medium, each medium with its reason, and does not report any tell as a ux-laws law finding or score
Says it did not render the result and marks the render-only evidence as source only
